pages.text: These glyphs further expand the practitioner’s tools for mathematical evaluation. Most of these glyphs concern themselves with trigonometry, useful for computing angles to create precise effects in real space.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.sin
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Takes a number, interprets it as an angle in degrees, and returns its corresponding sine value.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.cos
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Takes a number, interprets it as an angle in degrees, and returns its corresponding cosine value.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.tan
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Takes a number, interprets it as an angle in degrees, and returns its corresponding tangent value.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.asin
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Pops a number, takes its arcsine, and returns the result in degrees.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.acos
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Pops a number, takes its arccosine, and returns the result in degrees.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.atan
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Pops a number, takes its arctangent, and returns the result in degrees.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.atan2
pages.text: $(n)num, num$() → $(n)num$()$(br)A variant of arctangent that is sensitive to quadrant. Takes the head to be x, and the number below the head to be y, and evaluates for arctangent on the point (x, y).$(br)eg. y, x → the arctan of line corresponding to the point (x, y) on the unit circle

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.logab
pages.text: $(n)num, num$() → $(n)num$()$(br)Takes the logarithm of the number below the head with the number at the head as the base.$(br)eg. a, b → log of a with base b

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.to_radian
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Takes a number, interprets it as a value in degrees, and returns the corresponding value in radians.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.to_degree
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)number$()$(br)Takes a number, interprets it as a value in radians, and returns the corresponding value in degrees.
